expected.description:
Bang Average Football is the ultimate football game for fans of the beautiful (and sometimes not-so-beautiful) game!

Featuring fast-paced arcade matches and easy-to-learn mechanics, Bang Average Football is the perfect game for players of all skill levels. Choose from a range of men's and women's teams or design your own. Play with and against friends in local multiplayer or go for glory as both player and football manager in the single-player, RPG Story mode.

With simple controls and classic top-down arcade gameplay, Bang Average Football is the ultimate football experience!

Story Mode 

Join a washed-up, rock bottom football club as player… and instantly get promoted to the football manager position! As the player-manager, guide them through the ranks to the coveted top division.

Learn how to manage the whole football club: make transfers, upgrade the stadium, secure sponsorships, and engage with fans to maximise the club's all-important Reputation.

Visit other towns and football clubs around the country between matches, completing quests for NPCs and undertaking training drills to improve your abilities. Will you become National Champions and conquer the King’s Cup?  

Tournament Mode 

Create your own football tournament in a stand-alone mode! Make any combination of groups, divisions, and knockout rounds, using any mix of teams and settings, to construct and conquer your own competitions. Throw all your teams into one giant mega-league or recreate your favourite real-world football tournament from years gone by.

Steam Workshop & Custom Content 

Design your own player databases, and teams for Quick Matches and Tournaments, or personalise your Story mode hero with a variety of hairstyles and facial hair designs. Share your designs and football databases with others… and import the best football creations from around the world in seconds.

Features Local multiplayer for 1-4 players

25 teams and 1,000+ male and female players

Rich team and character creation tools

Deep tactical options, including custom formations and team instructions

Steam Workshop integration: share and download teams, leagues, tournaments, and more

Export replays as gifs with one click and immortalize your unbelievable top-bins efforts

Comprehensive accessibility settings, including button remapping, controller assists, and visual options including high contrast modes for colour blind players

installSteps.text: Alternatively, download Bang Average Football – Play, Manage, Create directly from the official site at https://www.ruairidx.com/bangaveragefootball. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.
Bang Average Football – Play, Manage, Create is also on Steam and is free there. Open the store page and press Play Game to add it to your library.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Check your distribution's package manager first, which is usually the easiest route. Otherwise download the AppImage from the official site, mark it executable and run it.

Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. Bang Average Football – Play, Manage, Create needs roughly 1.0 GB of free disk space.

set.tagline: A football club hands you the manager's job before checking whether you can pass.
set.description: Bang Average Football mixes brisk top-down football with an underdog player-manager story. Create teams and tournaments, tinker with formations, and share the couch with up to three friends for local co-op or versus matches.

systemRequirements.min: Windows: 64-bit Windows 7+, Intel Core i5/equivalent, 4 GB RAM, GTX 750/equivalent graphics, 1 GB storage. macOS: Mojave+, Apple M1 or Intel Core i5/equivalent, 4 GB RAM, Intel UHD 630, 1 GB storage. Linux: Intel Core i5/equivalent, 4 GB RAM, GTX 750/equivalent, 1 GB storage; Steam lists the OS as unspecified.
systemRequirements.recommended: Steam does not publish a distinct recommended CPU, RAM, GPU or storage tier for any supported OS.

min.cpuText: Windows/Linux: Intel Core i5 or equivalent; macOS: Apple M1 or Intel Core i5 or equivalent
min.gpuText: Windows/Linux: GeForce GTX 750 or equivalent; macOS: Intel UHD Graphics 630
min.notes: Steam lists Windows 7+, macOS Mojave+ and Linux with an unspecified distro. Current Steam client support on Windows begins at Windows 10.

recommended.notes: No distinct recommended hardware tier is published on Steam.

set.launcherInstall.note: Paid Steam game for Windows, macOS and Linux. Purchase and install in Steam, then use PlayBound Locate. It is not a free Steam download. Local co-op and versus are supported; PlayBound remote couch streaming is not yet verified for this game.

qualityBar.verdict: A scrappy top-down football game where the match ends and the club immediately hands you another problem to solve.

set.longDescription:
Bang Average Football opens with a club that needs help and an unlikely promotion: you arrive as a player and find yourself managing the place as well. The matches are fast, top-down and easy to read, but the season gives every win and missed tackle a consequence outside the pitch. You handle transfers, make tactical choices, improve the stadium and try to build a reputation for a team that has very little of one. It is the kind of football story where a routine fixture can feel important because you know what the club needs next.

Story Mode takes you between towns and teams, with errands and training drills alongside matches. You can alter formations and instructions, but the game does not ask you to spend an entire evening inside a spreadsheet before kicking off. Tournament Mode is more flexible: build groups, divisions or knockout brackets from the teams you want, then play through the competition. The creator tools let players make teams and databases of their own. Steam Workshop gives those creations a route between friends, while replay export can turn a spectacularly unlikely goal into a GIF before anyone argues that it never happened.

The multiplayer boundary matters. Steam lists one to four players in local co-op and versus modes, plus Remote Play Together. That is couch play or a stream of couch play, not a documented native online football lobby or dedicated server. PlayBound's own couch streaming could eventually give friends another path, but this specific game has not been verified in that flow yet. We should not advertise virtual LAN or automatic online-party joining from the word multiplayer alone. The game does include button remapping and controller assists, so native controller support is well supported by the developer's feature list. That is much better evidence than assuming every sports game supports pads.

The current Steam release is a paid purchase for Windows, macOS and Linux. The old Draft instructed players to press a free Play Game button and mentioned imaginary standalone DMG and AppImage files. Those steps have been replaced with the real Steam purchase and installation path. Steam publishes separate minimum hardware lines for all three platforms: 4 GB RAM and 1 GB storage throughout, but different CPU, graphics and OS details for Mac versus Windows and Linux. It publishes no distinct recommended tier. There is no need to invent one.

Bang Average Football's strongest move is making the person on the pitch responsible for the mess around it. A clean tackle may save the match; a good transfer might save next month. It is friendly enough for a quick couch tournament and substantial enough to make an underdog season feel like your own unlikely managerial career.
set.whyWePickedIt: The match play is immediately readable, and the player-manager career gives wins a reason to matter after the whistle. Four-player local modes, accessible controls and creation tools make it a natural fit for friends around a PC. Its Steam purchase and couch-only multiplayer scope are now stated plainly.
set.thatOneThing: You get promoted from player to manager so fast that the club has barely finished spelling your name on the team sheet.

installSteps.text: Buy Bang Average Football on Steam. Install the build for your OS through the Steam library, then use PlayBound Locate to select the installed game. This is a paid game, not a free download.
Use Steam's Windows build and keep Steam installed for ownership and updates. The Steam client requires a supported modern Windows version even though the game's listed minimum names Windows 7.
Use the macOS build in your Steam library. Steam lists macOS Mojave or later and Apple M1 or Intel Core i5-class hardware as its minimum.
Use the Linux build in your Steam library. Steam does not specify a Linux distribution in its minimum requirements.

firstPlaySteps.text: Choose Story Mode for the player-manager career or Tournament Mode for a custom competition. Remap controller buttons and assists in the accessibility options before starting a local match.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: For local co-op or versus, connect up to four players to one PC and choose a compatible match mode. Steam Remote Play Together can stream that local session to friends; PlayBound's own couch-stream path has not yet been verified for this title.
